instructions: Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic. Crumble the feta into a bowl. Pick 20 basil leaves.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until it's soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomato paste and the salt and stir for 1 minute, until the paste darkens.
Add the crushed tomatoes and 4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat.

Snap the spaghetti in half and add it to the pot. Stir well, turn the heat to medium so it bubbles steadily, and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes so it doesn't stick, until the pasta is just tender and the sauce has thickened.
Take the pot off the heat. Stir in two-thirds of the feta, the basil leaves and the pepper until most of the feta melts into the sauce.
Serve topped with the remaining feta.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: The Hungry Bites (a Greek site, no rating shown) is the only version found by this name, and it is the lead: onion, garlic and tomato paste cooked down, tomatoes and water, then the spaghetti cooked right in the sauce and finished with feta and basil. It uses fresh grated tomatoes and a 10 minute covered simmer; this uses canned crushed tomatoes and skips that simmer to stay near 30 minutes, and water in place of the optional chicken stock so it stays vegetarian. Quantities are scaled from 2 servings to 4, with the feta lowered from 200 g per 200 g of pasta to 8 oz for 12 oz.

sources.name: The Hungry Bites
